_meta.note: Default gate and grading-curve constants, single-sourced here so tuning is a config edit, not a code change. GateConfig reads these as its built-in defaults; an .impact-gate.yml and CLI flags still override per-repo.

absolute.note: Absolute composite-impact thresholds. Used when the curve is off, and as the fallback before a project baseline exists. null = that threshold is not set.

curve.note: Percentile-based grading. When enabled, a change is graded by its percentile against the blended (seed + project) distribution instead of a raw number. The graded value is always the composite (change-level) impact; per-file mutation cost is a ranking signal, not a rival gating metric.

cognitive.note: Absolute per-method Cognitive Complexity (Campbell 2018) gate, independent of the change-impact composite/curve. ON by default: any method in a changed file whose cognitive complexity exceeds this value is reported (and fails the build only when the cognitive measure is in 'block'). SonarSource's default line is 15; this gate is a touch more permissive at 20. Switch it off with enforcement 'off' for the cognitive measure.

measures.note: Per-measure enforcement override. All three measures (change_impact, cognitive, coupling) run by default and inherit the top-level 'enforcement' (warn) unless overridden here. 'off' turns a measure off entirely (not run, not reported); 'warn' reports only, never fails the build; 'block' fails the build when that measure fires. So nothing blocks on first use; turn blocking on for every measure with top-level 'enforcement: block', or for one measure by setting it here, and switch a measure off the same way.

baseline.note: How the merged history becomes the per-commit distribution. Walk the first-parent mainline of the merged base branch (only landed work; in-flight branches are never reached). One observation per atomic landed change: a main non-merge commit (its own diff); a leaf MR (net branch-start..tip); a parent MR's direct commits netted per run between merges, each based at the preceding synced base, with child MRs recursing and parent/main syncs skipped. A merge is never scored as its own diff, so a long-running roll-up cannot inflate the numbers. exclude_subject_pattern skips an MR by its merge-commit subject; max_commits caps how many recent mainline commits are walked.
